summary: Facts are held in memory by default, but cache plugins can store them for reuse across runs. Cached facts let you read another host's facts through hostvars even if that host hasn't run yet in the current play. They also allow patterns like nightly fact gathering for thousands of hosts.
questions: How can I reuse facts between playbook runs instead of regathering them?
How do I read another host's OS family from hostvars?
What cache plugin does Ansible use for facts by default?
Can fact caching speed things up for thousands of hosts?
Why can't I see another host's facts if it hasn't been contacted yet?

answer_card.title: Caching facts for reuse
answer_card.answer_md:
By default facts go to the `memory` cache plugin and last only for the current run. Choose a persistent cache plugin (see the cache plugins docs) to keep them.

With cached facts you can read other hosts' data even if they have not run yet:

```jinja
{{ hostvars['asdf.example.com']['ansible_facts']['os_family'] }}
```

A common pattern for large fleets is to gather facts nightly and then run smaller, more frequent configuration plays against the cache.
